on_label_indications: EXOGEN: non-invasive treatment of established nonunions excluding skull and vertebra

EXOGEN: accelerating healing of fresh, closed, posteriorly displaced distal radius fractures and fresh, closed or Grade I open tibial diaphysis fractures managed by closed reduction and cast immobilization in skeletally mature individuals

applications.evidence_summary: One-paragraph adjacent note. The TRUST trial (BMJ 2016, n=501, 43 North American centers, sham-controlled) found LIPUS did not accelerate radiographic healing or functional recovery after IM nailing of tibial fractures; a 2014 meta-analysis of 13 RCTs (737 patients) found no reduction in nonunion with PEMF or LIPUS in acute fractures. The PMA fresh-fracture indication is limited to cast-managed fractures and predates TRUST. Stimulators are not biologics and do not compete for the surgeon's graft decision, but they do compete for the nonunion-prevention budget and are the only nonunion product class with a dedicated HCPCS/DME payment.
applications.caveats: Negative Level I data for the operatively treated tibia; nonunion indication rests on older uncontrolled PMA data; industry-funded registries dominate the rest.
applications.challenge: TRUST is the trial a hiring manager will cite; the rep must know it and the 2020 label change.

applications.evidence_summary: Nonunion indication (established nonunion, excluding skull and vertebra) is based on self-controlled PMA series; no RCT against surgery.
applications.caveats: Uncontrolled evidence.

evidence.title: Re-evaluation of low intensity pulsed ultrasound in treatment of tibial fractures (TRUST): randomized clinical trial
evidence.finding: Sham-controlled, blinded, 43 centers; LIPUS did not improve radiographic healing or SF-36 physical component after operatively managed tibial fractures.

evidence.title: Effects of LIPUS and PEMF bone growth stimulation in acute fractures: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
evidence.finding: 13 trials; no significant difference in proportion of nonunion between PEMF/LIPUS and control.

bd.reimbursement: Durable medical equipment: HCPCS E0760 (ultrasound osteogenesis stimulator) and E0747 (electrical, non-spinal); Medicare NCD 150.2 covers LIPUS for nonunion with documented failure to progress on serial radiographs over at least 3 months (criteria to be re-verified); Orthofix 10-K notes bone growth therapy devices are exempt from DMEPOS competitive bidding and that CMS has considered prior authorization.
bd.notes: Adjacent-only record per the atlas brief. Sales model is DME prescription and prior-authorization support, a different channel from the operating room.

products.name: Teriparatide (Forteo and generics/biosimilars) for nonunion, off-label
products.company: Eli Lilly (Forteo); Teva, Alvogen/Bonsity, Apotex generics
products.ownership_history: Forteo approved 2002 for osteoporosis; US generics from 2019-2020 (Teva, Bonsity); the 2-year lifetime limit was removed from the label in 2020.
products.composition: Recombinant human PTH(1-34), 20 mcg subcutaneous daily

regulatory.reference: NDA 021318 (Drugs@FDA: NDA, not a BLA) (Forteo, 2002); nonunion/fracture-healing use is off-label
on_label_indications: Osteoporosis at high risk of fracture (postmenopausal women, men, glucocorticoid-induced); no fracture-healing or nonunion indication

applications.evidence_summary: Short pharmacologic note. Evidence for nonunion is case reports and small series: a 20-patient Italian multicenter series reported 85% of delayed/nonunions healed by 6 months of off-label teriparatide; a 40-patient comparative study of Ilizarov with or without teriparatide in septic tibial nonunion found shorter frame time. No RCT in established nonunion; the fracture-healing RCTs (distal radius, pelvis) showed modest or no effect on the primary endpoints.
applications.caveats: Off-label, osteosarcoma boxed-warning history (removed 2020), cost; outcomes in series are uncontrolled. Not a device-company product; relevant to BD as a prescribing trend that competes with surgical biologics in osteoporotic nonunion.
applications.challenge: Do not overstate; 'adjunct a surgeon might prescribe' is the honest framing.

evidence.title: Use of teriparatide in preventing delayed bone healing and nonunion: multicentric study on a series of 20 patients
evidence.finding: Off-label 6-month course with or without surgery; healing progression in 80% at 3 months and 85% healed at 6 months.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of teriparatide combined with the Ilizarov technique in septic tibial non-union
evidence.finding: Ilizarov with vs without teriparatide in ASAMI type C septic nonunions; teriparatide group had less time in frame (p<0.05); clinical outcome scores similar.

bd.reimbursement: Pharmacy benefit (Part D / commercial); off-label nonunion use is typically denied or needs appeal; generics reduced cost substantially.
bd.notes: Included only as the pharmacologic comparator.

products.name: LDGraft (controlled-release rhBMP-2 on degradable polymer scaffold)
products.ownership_history: Spun out of University of Nottingham; venture-backed; FDA Breakthrough Device designation May 2023 for single-level ALIF L3-S1; FDA IDE approval September 2025 expanding the RESTORE study to US sites.
products.composition: rhBMP-2 encapsulated in a degradable polymer (ReGenerOs/TAOS platform) for sustained low-dose release rather than burst release from collagen sponge

regulatory.reference: Breakthrough Device designation May 2023 (single-level ALIF, L3-S1, DDD); FDA IDE approval announced 2025-09-08. ClinicalTrials.gov has two LDGraft records: NCT06462729 (Locate Bio Pty Ltd; Phase 1/2, ALIF, n=40 estimated; IDE-flagged unapproved device; recruiting since 2024-11-12; sites in Newcastle, Australia and Fort Wayne, Nashville and Pinehurst, US; last update 2026-08-26) and NCT07858643 (Locate Bio Ltd; 'AMBITION', n=25, sites in Tbilisi, Georgia; started 2026-04-08). NCT06462729 is the registration that matches the Australia-plus-US IDE study.
on_label_indications: Investigational: single-level ALIF for degenerative disc disease (spine); no trauma indication proposed

applications.evidence_summary: No trauma program announced; included because a controlled-release BMP-2 would be the natural successor to Infuse in open fractures and nonunion if the spine study succeeds.
applications.caveats: Spine-only development; no trauma data.

pipeline.expected_milestone: RESTORE study US enrollment from late 2025 (company release, September 2025); no PMA timeline public.

bd.reimbursement: None.
bd.notes: Watch item for anyone building a trauma BMP thesis; the IP angle is dose reduction, which addresses the inflammation/seroma issues that limited Infuse.

products.challenge: Two separate registrations exist; the Australia-plus-US IDE study is NCT06462729. The sponsor's 'RESTORE' name was not seen on either record.

products.name: OSTEOGROW / OSTEOGROW-C (rhBMP6 in autologous blood coagulum)
products.company: Genera Research Ltd (Zagreb, Croatia) with Perform Biologics (US affiliate)
products.ownership_history: Originated in the EU FP7 OSTEOGROW project (grant 279239, 2012-2017, coordinator University of Zagreb, EU contribution EUR 5.68 million); Genera Research holds the IP (company states patents to 2043).
products.composition: Recombinant human BMP6 bound to an autologous whole-blood-coagulum carrier (WBCD), with or without allograft/ceramic particles (OSTEOGROW-C)

regulatory.reference: No US IDE/IND or registry entry found; EU phase I/II trials in distal radius fracture and HTO were conducted under the FP7 project; company materials cite over 300 patients treated and a Phase III protocol approval targeted for March 2027
on_label_indications: Investigational: fracture nonunion, HTO gap healing, distal radius fracture, dental (company list)

applications.evidence_summary: EU-funded phase I/II in HTO distraction-gap healing and distal radius fractures (CORDIS project page describes plans; peer-reviewed phase II results were not retrieved in this sweep). ClinicalTrials.gov search for OSTEOGROW/rhBMP6 returned nothing.
applications.caveats: Company-reported status only; no registry or FDA footprint found.
applications.challenge: Verify any trial claim against EU CTIS before citing.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase III in nonunion is a stated plan, not a registered trial.
applications.caveats: Unverified.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Company states Phase III protocol regulatory approval expected March 2027 (BIO 2026 exhibitor profile); unverified.

bd.reimbursement: None.
bd.notes: Scientific interest (BMP6 is less inhibited by noggin and the blood carrier avoids collagen) but the commercial organization is thin; a BD lead would treat it as a licensing target, not a competitor.

products.challenge: EU register results for the PLIF trial (2017-000860-14, posted 11 Feb 2026) were read on 2026-10-22; see the spine.json osteogrow record for the posted proportions and the unit-error caveat.

products.name: NVD-003 (autologous adipose-derived osteogenic 3D graft)
products.ownership_history: Spun out of UCLouvain (2013); FDA Orphan Drug and Rare Pediatric Disease designations for congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (December 2020), RMAT designation, IND (March 2021); Phase 3 in CPT started September 2025.
products.composition: Autologous adipose-derived stem cells differentiated into a scaffold-free 3D osteogenic implant with HA/beta-TCP particles (3M3 platform); manufactured per patient

regulatory.reference: IND (2021); Orphan Drug and Rare Pediatric Disease designations (2020); RMAT; eligible for a priority review voucher if approved
on_label_indications: Investigational: congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (pediatric, Paley type 3-4 diaphyseal); recalcitrant lower-limb nonunion in adults

applications.evidence_summary: Adult phase 1/2 in recalcitrant lower-limb nonunion (NCT06335394, n=11 enrolled, company reported 9 treated): clinical healing in 8/9 at 2 years, median 6 months, no implant-related complications (company release, December 2022). Pediatric CPT Phase 3 vs ICBG (NCT07112443, n=12, 7 sites US/EU, primary completion October 2026) is recruiting.
applications.caveats: Tiny uncontrolled adult series; company-reported; the Phase 3 is powered as an orphan study (n=12). Manufacturing is autologous and weeks-long, unsuited to acute trauma.
applications.challenge: Orphan CPT is a route to a BLA, not a trauma market; the adult nonunion path would need a separate pivotal.

evidence.title: Phase 3 randomized controlled study of NVD003 vs iliac crest bone graft in pediatric congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia
evidence.finding: Recruiting at Phoenix Children's, Loma Linda, Sinai Baltimore, Mayo, Brussels, Amiens, Barcelona; primary endpoint overall healing at 12 months (mRUST 13 or more, no pain on weight bearing, no secondary intervention).

evidence.title: Single-arm study of NVD-003 for recalcitrant lower limb nonunion in adults
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; company reported 8/9 clinical healing at 2 years.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Phase 3 primary completion October 2026, study completion July 2027 (ClinicalTrials.gov); BLA timing not public.

bd.reimbursement: Would be a biologic (BLA) with potential for separate payment; none today.
bd.notes: Sister product NVD-X3 (allogeneic) has an IND for cervical fusion (2024). The priority review voucher is the financial story.

products.name: ALLOB (allogeneic osteoblastic cell therapy) - failed
products.ownership_history: Bone Therapeutics (Gosselies) developed ALLOB and PREOB; reverse merger with Medsenic created BioSenic (2022); ALLOB Phase IIb in tibial fracture failed (June 2023); company pivoted to oral arsenic trioxide and later licensed/returned ALLOB rights amid a terminated Pregene license (2023).
products.composition: Allogeneic bone-marrow MSCs differentiated to osteoblastic lineage, cryopreserved, injected percutaneously

regulatory.reference: EU ATMP trials (EudraCT 2018-001054-96); no US IND found
on_label_indications: None; development discontinued

applications.evidence_summary: Phase IIb (n=57 treated) in acute tibial fractures at risk of delayed union gave ALLOB days after injury; it failed to accelerate healing and BioSenic suspended the program (June 2023), concluding MSCs should not be given in the acute inflammatory window. An earlier mid-phase delayed-union study had been positive.
applications.caveats: Negative RCT; informative for anyone proposing early cell therapy in acute fracture.
applications.challenge: Cited as the reason cell therapy in acute trauma is out of favor.

evidence.title: Bone Therapeutics' final asset buried after failure in phase 2 fracture study (Fierce Biotech)
evidence.finding: ALLOB did not accelerate fracture healing in the Phase IIb; safety acceptable; program suspended.

bd.reimbursement: None.
bd.notes: Case study for diligence: a cell therapy with positive delayed-union signal that failed when moved to acute fracture.

products.name: OssiGraft / OssiGraft Prime viable bone matrix

applications.evidence_summary: First case was an ankle surgery (2023); no published outcomes; no trauma data.

products.company: Ferring Pharmaceuticals (sponsor of pivotal); originally BioSET Inc

bd.reimbursement: None.
bd.notes: Peptide-on-ceramic is the same construct class as i-Factor (P-15); that is the comparator a hiring manager will raise.

products.company: Various (Elute, RTI Surgical, Artoss, SDIP Innovations, Stryker, SurGenTec, Anika, Acuitive)
products.ownership_history: Tracker record, not a single product.
products.composition: Mixed: synthetic resorbable calcium salts, nanocrystalline HA, citrate-based polymer/ceramic (CITREPORE), hyaluronic-acid-based injectable, moldable allograft

regulatory.reference: K241555 RTI Surgical Moldable Bone Void Filler (2025-02-21, RTI Surgical, Inc.); K250346 Elute BonVie+ (2025-02-26, Elute, Inc.); K250521 NanoBone SBX Putty / NanoBone QD (2025-04-07, applicant Biocomposites, Ltd., which owns Artoss/NanoBone); K252797 JAZBI Resorbable Bone Void Filler (2026-05-26, SDIP Innovations Pty Ltd); K261008 Vitoss BiModal foam strip family (2026-04-24, Stryker Spine); K240450 Citrepore (2024-11-06, Acuitive Technologies); SurGenTec OsteoFlo HydroFiber K242797 (2024-12-23), K243949 (2025-05-28), K251720 (2025-07-02); Anika Tactoset Injectable Bone Substitute K212083 (2021-08-31), K231968 (2023-12-20); Fibergraft BG Putty GPS K253147 (2025-10-22, Prosidyan)

applications.caveats: Bench-only clearances; the list was built from product-code listings and may be incomplete.

evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion December 2026.

evidence.finding: Not yet recruiting; start October 2026.

products.name: Opening-wedge osteotomy ceramic wedges (Arthrex HATriC, OSferion; Cross.Bone)
products.ownership_history: HATriC cleared to Arthrex 2004 (K040381); OSferion (Olympus Terumo Biomaterials beta-TCP) distributed by Arthrex as an osteotomy wedge; Cross.Bone wedge K071876.
products.composition: HATriC: 60% HA / 40% beta-TCP biphasic ceramic wedge; OSferion: 100% high-purity beta-TCP wedge

regulatory.reference: K040381 (HATriC, 2004-05-12); K071876 (Cross.Bone wedge, tibial osteotomy with internal fixation); OSferion wedge K number not retrieved
on_label_indications: Bone void filler or bone graft substitute in bony voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (extremities, pelvis, spine); not a load-bearing device; use with adequate post-operative immobilization (HATriC)

applications.evidence_summary: Beta-TCP and HA/TCP wedges fill large opening-wedge gaps with locking plates; meta-analyses show no overall nonunion difference vs no filler or graft, and a 2026 systematic review of 1,640 knees found no outcome benefit from any filler for gaps under 10 mm. A 2026 bilateral-knee RCT (n=42) found TCP granules gave better WOMAC/VAS than allograft.
applications.caveats: Clearance is for a void filler with a 'not load-bearing' statement, while the clinical use is structural gap support under a plate; cleared without clinical data.

evidence.title: The use of bone void fillers may not impact outcomes after medial opening wedge HTO: systematic review
evidence.finding: 28 studies; 36% allograft, 30% no filler, 22% synthetic, 12% autograft; no outcome difference; fillers may add complications for gaps under 10 mm.

evidence.title: Allogenous bone graft versus synthetic calcium-phosphate graft in opening wedge HTO
evidence.finding: 84 knees (bilateral), randomized by knee; TCP granules superior on WOMAC and VAS at 2.1 years; consolidation 54.8%; no loss of correction.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled inpatient MS-DRG or packaged into the outpatient osteotomy APC (HTO is increasingly outpatient).
bd.notes: Sold as a system accessory with Arthrex's osteotomy plates; evidence says the plate, not the wedge, is doing the work.
